To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a new class of solid state electrolyte based on ionic liquids impregnated metal-organic frameworks, which shows high ionic conductivity, high compatibility with both Li metal and LiFePO4, and low interfacial resistance.

the unique wetting effect of the ionic liquid guests in the MOF nanocrystals creates an effective ionic conductive network throughout Li metal anode and LiFePO4 cathode, which results in a high performance SSB with a high loading and high energy density.

a novel solid-like electrolyte based on ionic liquids impregnated metal-organic-framework nanocrystals (MOFs) has been reported, which exhibits high ionic conductivity, high Li+ transference numbers, good compatibility with active electrodes, and high energy density for solid-state Li metal batteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new type of solid like electrolyte based on ionic liquids confined in nanocrystals of a metal organic framework.
the development of a novel SLE based on ionic liquids confined in MOF nanocrystals for high energy density SSBs, which could be a promising strategy for the design of advanced SSBs.
the development of a novel Li IL@MOFs based solid electrolyte, which is expected to be a promising candidate for high energy density SSBs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Li IL@MOFs SLE with nanowetted interfaces is a promising electrolyte for high energy density SSBs.

a novel solid like SLE is developed, which is composed of Li IL impregnated MOF nanocrystals, which demonstrates excellent compatibility with both Li metal and LiFePO4 active electrodes, and thus achieves a high active loading of 2.5 mAh cm 2 and high energy density of 1.2 mWh cm 2.
the Li IL@MOFs SLEs are promising candidates for SSBs with high energy density and good safety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanowetted interfaces in Li IL@MOFs SLEs are promising for high energy density solid state batteries.
the nanowetted interface of the Li IL@MOFs based SLE is a promising strategy to improve the interfacial kinetics and thus the performance of SSB.
the Li IL@MOFs SLEs provide an effective way to achieve higher energy density solid state lithium batteries by creating nanowetted interfaces between the electrolyte and the active electrodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SLE with nanowetted interfaces is promising for high performance solid state batteries.
by combining the advantages of MOF and IL, a new type of SLE is developed, and the unique nanowetting effect at the interface between the SLE, Li metal, and electrode materials is demonstrated.

a high performance solid state electrolyte can be designed by integrating ionic liquid with a metal organic framework, which provides a new strategy to develop advanced solid state electrolytes for energy storage applications.
